[2026-06-26 21:09] vachacz : Guys, just wondering what to build next:  1. Someone suggested ability to play friendly games and I consider this not only entertaining but also helpful in terms of engine calibration. More games = more feedback. We could allow one not-rated game per day played 8am instead of leagues played 8pm. Basically select a team and click "invite for a friendly" which arranges a friendly in the first possible slot free for all teams. Friendly wouldn't apply fatigue / exp / team record / player stats. Just a pure game. We could also add "auto accept invitations" which basically allows to agree to friendlies right away. Otherwise you'd recieve a notification about friendly game offer.  2. Some in-game social features such as private league chat so that people not joining discord could interact with each other  3. New skills ... we discussed about driving/ball handling. I do think that something like that could be missing a bt. I just imagine Doncic skills and I miss exarly that to express his skill in the game. One skill wouldn't ruin current UI so maybe this is the right choice  4. National leagues suggested by <@998763559439843348>. Ofc this is a must have but I think it's too early. We need more players.  5. Maybe play-offs which are kinda natural to basketball. This comes with some tradeoffs which can be hard to overcome. Basically play-offs mean that some teams need to wait until playoffs are over. I don't consider this as an urgent thing is current season flow works well.  6. Team spirit, team confidence, and fan mood. This could be nice but it's rather a minor thing. Cherry on top.  7. Player personalities and sort of psychology. I personally think that it's one of the last featues. Instead player perks could be nteresting https://discord.com/channels/1510571165469642883/1517981308079313136/1517991497415262290  What's your opinion @everyone ?

[2026-06-26 22:28] pubke : Hi, it is pretty funny. I am also working on a basketball manager game. Yours is definitely better at the moment haha. I also loved playing Charazay years ago and now I want to make something similar. Just for fun for now 😄
[2026-06-26 23:29] dcarra. : Overall I like the direction here—these are the kind of systems that can shape the long-term depth of the game—but I’d prioritise them a bit differently and expand a couple of the ideas. 1. Friendlies system Really good idea,  it can help both engagement and engine tuning. I’d also consider: optionally giving reduced XP / training progression (even if no stats/record impact), otherwise it risks being purely cosmetic and quickly ignored adding a simple fatigue toggle (full / reduced / none) so it can be used for experimentation vs casual games a lightweight matchmaking layer (similar strength teams preferred, but still open invites possible) “auto-accept friendlies” is a great QoL feature, especially if activity increases This could become a really important sandbox/testing tool over time. 2. In-game communication Strong yes. A basic league chat / match chat system is almost mandatory  3. New skill (ball handling / driving) I agree this is probably the missing piece. Right now it feels like we’re lacking a way to express “Luka Doncic-type” creativity. Even a single new attribute like: ball handling / driving / creation under pressure could unlock a lot of identity without overcomplicating the UI. 4. National teams Great long-term feature, but I agree it’s early. The main blockers I see: we need larger player pool first and especially better youth generation quality + variance Also national teams would need clear rules for selection (form, potential, nationality locks, etc.), otherwise it becomes chaotic quickly. 5. Playoffs Personally I’m neutral as well. It’s natural for basketball, but: it adds complexity to season flow and scheduling could create “dead time” for eliminated teams Not urgent, but could be revisited once leagues feel more stable and populated. 6.
[2026-06-26 23:29] dcarra. : Team spirit / confidence / fan mood I’d keep this as low priority core-wise, but fan systems could actually become interesting if expanded properly. Instead of just a “mood value”, it could connect to: ticket pricing elasticity attendance fluctuations merchandising revenue sponsor expectations / bonuses That would create a nice economy loop without affecting match simulation too much. 7. Player personalities / psychology Agree this is “later stage”. It’s depth, not foundation. I’d strongly prefer starting with perk-based identity systems first (simpler, clearer impact), and only later moving into deeper personality/psych layers when the core systems are fully stable.

[2026-06-27 14:02] vachacz : @everyone important update. <@442801289592700928> and <@910880362937331742> reported some weired games and after looking into them I have a few conclusions  - even if a game should be teoretically won this is sport and chances are never 100%-0% but sometimes 60%-40% somtimes 80%-20%. it means you can loose a game which looks easy - such loose can be because of bad luck or because of issue with the engine and this is something we have to figure our first. always! - to move forward instead of analysing provided games I implemented a backoffice tool which will simulate the same game up to 1000 times and provide statistics (%win / %lost and many others) - such tools is really prerequisite to assess if we have a problem or not - to allows such analysis I will make db snapshots of entire rooster incl. fatigue before the game to allow such x1000 fairness check. such tests will tell us what to improve and what is just bad luck  tools and required snapshot mechanism goes live later today. hope it will help as move forward fast  btw. as you can see some random game simulated locally gave 65%-35% win chances and stat curves does not look bad at all when rolled up to 1000 games. it convinces me that the direction is good

[2026-07-13 17:29] lucadrago5 : Reading the explanations about rebounding, it's the only skill that, unlike the others, has pros and cons. From what's described, it's much better to have high rebounds in big men than to have an average one in everyone. A player over 2m gains 1.8% for every cm, while the opposite is true for players under 2m. So it's all a calculation, but unlike other games, as it's described, it's a skill that particularly enhances players based on their role and height. You risk paying a point guard a lot to have 80 rebounds, but then if he's particularly short, it becomes almost useless. 80 for a 2m player is 80. For a 190m player it's 66. 210 -> 94. Then it counts even more if you put it C->Pf->Sf->Sg->Pg

[2026-08-13 15:59] dcarra. : I’d like to share a couple of thoughts about the starting teams after the reset.  Since one of the main reasons for the reset is to improve the overall balance between teams, I’m wondering whether the current ranges for bench players — 21–31 years old and potential between 3 and 9 — might actually introduce too much randomness into the initial setup, rather than ensuring that teams start from a reasonably equal position.  For example, a very lucky manager could end up with three players under 23, all with high potential, while an unlucky manager could get a bench made up mostly of players over 26, with relatively low potential. Even if the teams have the same number of players and roughly comparable starting values, the long-term potential could be dramatically different simply because of the random generation.  I’m definitely in favour of having some randomness. I don’t think every starting roster should be identical, because having some variation makes the game more interesting and gives managers something to work with. However, I feel that the current range might be too wide, especially considering that we're specifically trying to achieve better balance with this reset.  One possible solution would be to reduce the range, making it more similar to what we have for the starting players. Another option would be to introduce some kind of "total potential value" for the bench.  For example, if there are five bench players, we could establish a total potential value — let's say somewhere around 30–35, just as an example — and then distribute that value randomly among the five players.   You could still end up with one player having potential 3 and another having potential 9, which is perfectly fine. The important thing is that it would be much harder for one manager to randomly get young high potential players while another ends up with  old players with potential < 5.
[2026-08-13 16:00] dcarra. : The other point I'd like to understand better is how the two junior players added to the roster are generated.  I understand that their development is simulated using a certain Academy level — I believe 60 — but I'm wondering how random the actual players are. Can they essentially have any potential value?  This matters quite a lot as well. A very lucky manager could potentially get a junior with extremely high potential, while another manager could get two players with much lower potential. Again, that's not necessarily a problem by itself, because some randomness is healthy, but when combined with the randomness of the starting roster, it can potentially create quite a significant advantage right from day one.  I'm bringing this up mainly because I think we should try to avoid repeating some of the imbalance we're already seeing. Obviously, if we completely eliminate randomness, we also eliminate part of what makes each team unique. And I'm not suggesting that we need to make every starting player identical or completely remove the possibility of getting lucky.  My point is more about controlling the extremes. We can keep a meaningful random component while putting some limits in place so that the difference between the luckiest and unluckiest starting teams isn't too significant.   That's just my opinion, though. I'm curious to hear what everyone else thinks.

[2026-08-19 16:27] vachacz : @everyone I'm looking at the economy and I want to propose couple of changes. this is early draft  **Status quo** - savings with 7 friendlies a week, no academy investment is almost **5M**/season - savings with 7 friendlies, 200k academy + avg 2 medical tests is **2.8M** - pure friendly games are **1,8M** a season  **Proposed changes:** ⚠️ Objective: make academy cheaper to discourage pure cash collection and reduce overall savings to prevent inflation keeping the game attractive for newcomers. remove non intuitive scout report cost x2 more expensive than total salary cost ⚠️ due to slightly lower starting skills base salaries would slighly drop   - reduce friendly income by **30%** to **1M** - change max academy investment to **100k** to motivate for this investment - double the salaries **120k** after reset to **240k**  **Outcomes of the change:** - savings with 7 friendlies, no academy investment up to **3.1M** - savings with 7 friendlies and 100k academy investment + avg 2 medial tests is **2M** - savings with no friendlies, 100k academy investment + avg 2 medial tests exact **1M**  **Future changes** - non-linear salaries (as all team start with similar skills it can wait) - sponsor income depending on division hardiness (same as above, everyone starts the same)   **Still considered (likely to be implemented)** - additional income for playing homegrown players (not more than **500k**) - additional stuff (likely post reset topic)  Let's open discussion about that
[2026-08-19 17:52] rene779 : I like the reduction in income from friendly matches, because right now there is a strong incentive to play as many friendlies as possible simply for the additional income.  For that reason, I would even consider reducing the income from friendlies further, or potentially removing it altogether. In return, there could be more income from normal sponsors, home games, and/or match-win bonuses (see the suggestion below).  Friendlies are already very beneficial even without additional income, because they allow you to gain extra experience and test different team tactics without the same competitive pressure as league matches.
[2026-08-19 17:53] rene779 : ⸻  Why not add additional spending mechanisms to reduce inflation and discourage excessive saving?  1. Medical Staff Department  Similar to the youth scout system, you could introduce a medical staff department where players can invest money to improve their team’s medical capabilities.  Higher investment could, for example: * Reduce the recovery time after injuries. * Reduce the likelihood of players getting injured. * Potentially allow for more aggressive playing styles, depending on the weekly matchups. * Improve medical assessments of youth players, making it possible to evaluate their potential more accurately before signing them.   2. Trainer Staff  Another option could be a trainer staff system.  Trainers could work similarly to players: they would have different skills/stats, be randomly generated, appear on the transfer market, and could be signed for a transfer fee and then paid a weekly salary.  The basic idea would be that the greater the difference between a trainer’s skill in a specific area and the player’s current skill in that area, the stronger the training effect would be.  It could also be possible to employ multiple trainers. However, each additional trainer would increase the team’s fixed weekly expenses.  This would create an interesting management decision: Do you spend more money on several trainers to develop specific player attributes, or do you keep your expenses low and save the money instead?  Trainers could also age and eventually retire or leave the club after, for example, 5–6 seasons. This would create a continuous demand for new trainers and keep the system dynamic.  Overall, this would make saving money just one possible management strategy rather than the obvious choice. Managers who choose to spend more could gain advantages through faster player development and potentially stronger teams, while managers who prioritize saving would have more financial security but potentially slower development and fewer tactical options.
[2026-08-19 17:56] rene779 : ⸻  Possible Future Addition (Suggestion):  Season-Based Sponsor Options  In addition to the suggestions above, I think sponsor choices could become another interesting strategic decision each season.  This would need to be balanced very carefully, but I could imagine three different sponsor types:  1. Performance-Based Sponsor * Low base income * Moderate win bonus * Potentially the best option for teams that expect to win 80%+ of their games * Higher risk: if the team performs poorly, the total income could be lower than with the other options  2. Balanced Sponsor * Medium base income * Small win bonus * The most attractive option for teams with an expected win rate of roughly 30–80% * If a team performs within this range, this sponsor would provide a better overall return than the other two options  3. Safe/Guaranteed Sponsor * High base income * Very small or no win bonus * The best option for teams expecting to lose 30% or more of their games * Particularly useful for newcomers to a league or new players who are competing in a strong league  This would give managers another strategic decision each season: Do I want to take a financial risk in exchange for potentially higher income, choose a balanced option, or prioritize guaranteed income?  Combined with lower friendly income and additional ways to invest money into the club, this could help reduce inflation while creating more meaningful long-term management decisions.  - And sorry for this ultra long post!🙏   If it is too much, i can also delete it, or post it in another thread!

[2026-09-12 09:49] br0kh3n : Additional Financial Rewards  To further motivate Team Managers who invest in roster improvements, we propose two incentives: a Weekly Statistical Bonus and a Seasonal Sponsorship Reward.  Weekly Bonus for Top Statistical Players   Each week, the Manager whose player ranks #1 in a key category (Points, Rebounds, Assists, Steals, Blocks, or other official stats) earns a financial bonus. This rewards roster-building and player-development decisions that deliver measurable results, encouraging managers to invest in stronger players and nurture young talent. The better the roster, the greater the chance to earn.  Seasonal Sponsorship Reward   At season’s end, Managers receive a sponsorship reward for maintaining and developing a successful player. Sponsorship continues as long as the player remains in the League, but ends if transferred elsewhere.  Exceptions:  1) Promotion to another League does not interrupt sponsorship. 2)Market transfers within the same League also continue. This distinction ensures competitive progression is rewarded, not penalized.  Why Add These Rewards?   These incentives link roster investment, player development, competition, and financial gain. Managers who improve their rosters gain opportunities to recover part of their investment through player achievements.  It creates a healthy cycle: Invest in roster → Develop players → Compete for stats → Retain success → Earn rewards.  Weekly bonuses recognize short-term excellence, while seasonal sponsorships reward long-term management. Together, they make roster improvement financially meaningful without diminishing competition or strategy.  Principle:   Invest in your roster. Develop your players. Compete for the top. Earn from their success.  -edit- with witty parody-style sponsor names inspired by real-life products but cleverly tied to league achievements. Example: Top Blocker → ShieldGuard RoofSeal™ Top Assist → FiberFast Connections™ Top Steals → SnatchPro Security™ Top Rebounder → Mattress™
[2026-09-12 11:31] rene779 : To me this sounds more like an unhealthy cycle… Isn’t this just a snowballing effect?  You have the best player (in any category), you get money, you can solidify your lead (by investing in more individually strong players) even better.  I think this proposal leaves out the teams that play more like „teams“, rather than individually strong players.
[2026-09-12 12:21] br0kh3n : I see the concern about a possible snowball effect, but these rewards are meant to enhance engagement without destabilizing the League. Weekly bonuses rotate across multiple stat categories, giving different managers chances to win, while seasonal sponsorships reward consistency and player development — not just star power. Most importantly, the actual reward size hasn’t even been defined; it could be modest, such as covering the cost of one staff member per week, with seasonal rewards equal to or only slightly larger than weeklyTeam Sponsorship. In other words, the scale is flexible and can be set by the developers to ensure balance. Rather than creating an unhealthy cycle, this system provides measured incentives that make roster investment and teamwork financially meaningful, while keeping competition fair and strategic.

[2026-10-22 15:40] isr_shay : Yes, but I think he has a valid point. In my opinion, there should be some restrictions. I would suggest   1. limiting transfers to 10 per season (the exact number is up to the development team and can be adjusted). However, it's important to remember that both buying and selling a player should count as a transfer. If some teams are constantly flipping players and making 50 transfers per season, it can make it harder for other teams to progress and may also discourage new players from joining or staying in the game. I think some reasonable limits would help keep the game fair, balanced, and welcoming to new managers.  2. Instead of limiting the number of transfers per season, we could introduce a progressive tax based on how many players a team sells during a season.    For example:    - 1–10 sales: 5% tax (current rate)    - 11–20 sales: 12% tax    - 21–30 sales: 20% tax    - 31+ sales: 35% tax     This way, regular managers won't be affected, while teams making 50–60 transfers per season for profit will face higher costs.    It won't prevent trading, but it will make excessive player flipping less profitable while keeping the transfer market open to everyone.    The numbers are just examples and can be adjusted by the development team.

[2026-06-30 20:56] vachacz : @everyone first engine decision ahead. As promised I will consult with you in this new channel entirely focused on engine calibration:  It can happen that your active lineup has injured players or player gets injured or fouled out during the game. In that case current engine makes a replacement decision by replacing unavailable players with players on similar position. You have no influence on that and it can lead to suboptimal decisions from manager perspective. My question is what would you prefer: **Leave it to the engine or let player define squad depth?**.  Something like on the mockup.  Edge cases: - 2nd C playing 10 minutes gets injured. Your first backup is 1st C already scheduled for 30 minutes. As a consequence primary C plays 40 minutes. As we're taking about emergency situation I wouldn't overcomplicate by adding additional logic. **Is it ok to rely on depth chart without additional rules?**
[2026-06-30 20:58] vachacz : And immediately second question which was already discussed. **Should players get penalty for playing on non-nominal positions or the only penalty should be because of the size/bmi and skills?**  I'm hesitating on that. My arguments: - typically PG is trained to handle the ball, make passes so when suddenly he is sent to play as C typical moves on this position (pivots, position fight) may not be natural for a PG. This makes me think that PG playing on C should have a penalty. Same applies to all position swaps. - on the other hand it might be enough to say that PG is smaller than opponents C and will get a penalty for hight/wieght anyways  If we implement 1st option I would define a cleat penlty matrix for each swap.

[2026-07-06 18:49] vachacz : ℹ️ @everyone short update about the engine progress. i slowed down a bit to review the architecture and made bunch of important decisions which will have long term consequences:  - as we're in the beta changes to the engine could be done quickly but once the engine is stable and lots of players get used to it changes will have to be gradual and transparent which stays in big conflict with ad-hoc fixes possible in beta. i see the future as follows     - engine v1 running in league games and v2 with minor fixes running in friendly games      - activation of v2 for league games between seasons     - both v1 and v2 tested against single test suite     - v1 and v2 can be verified against each other by running 1000's of games and finding what is the "statistical" impact  - in the end it's all about transparency for players and predictability of the game. not following that is against my vision how the game works  - to support all of that approach I have to provide option to run mutliple engines in parallel which was not designed upfront. I'm refactoring the code to allow that also for upcoming engine tweaks  in parallel I'm crafting v2 engine specs. I will publish them in coming days. for now I can only reveal a bit what is **NOT** working in current engine  - ball handling has no impact (this skill was added few days ago after our discussions so it's not suprising for those who are here for +1-2 weeks) - athetism has almost no impact (some of you noticed that already) - weight and BMI have no impact - block formulas are flat and needs to be fixed - free throws are not balanced well with fouls. we had games with some extreme imbalace  To summarise: solid engineering matters 😉 if you're interested in more details happy to even host a short meet about that 😉
[2026-07-07 18:27] vachacz : @everyone let me reveal a bit what I've been working on in background. something you can have a look at. this is just a starting point  I attach a html spec file for sanity tests of the engine. Purpose is that no changes to production will be possible without passing all sanity tests in that file. Everything is automated. Tests are devided in groups and for sure are not perfect yes. I'd say 80% ready. Tests are devided into groups  - T2 group: what overall stat numbers are ok - T3 group: how results and stats react if we bump entire team by +5/+10/+15/+20 - T4 group: how results and stats react if we bump just one skill - T5 group: how form/fatige/exp impact win rates - T7 group: rebound shares  and few more. i run let's say 200 simulations for each test and check if combined conditions fits the expectation. if everything is green it's a guardrail for future engine tweaks. current engine passes 90/130 tests. same are failing as expected (ball handling, ath) but some are surprising.  next I preceed with improving the engine

[2026-07-09 21:47] vachacz : @everyone New **v2** match engine in friendlies just got enabled   League games still use the classic engine for now; friendlies are your first look at version 2.  **What stays the same** Form, weekly fatigue, experience, lineups, tactics sliders, fouls, free throws, and the box score you already know. Your roster still has the same eight trainable skills and the same aggression, shot focus, and pass-vs-shot settings.  **Every skill can move the score** In the v1 engine, ball handling and athleticism barely changed results. In v2 they do — through turnovers, rebounding, blocks, steals, and paint play.  **Passing reaches the scoreboard** Higher passing raises how often a shot is an assisted look. Player assisted by a good passer gets a shooting bonus; assists are credited only when that shot goes in. Good passers lift team shooting and points, not just assist totals.  **Ball handling reaches the scoreboard** Stronger ball handling cuts dribble turnovers and nudges the offense toward more paint attempts. Players with better handles are more likely to take and finish those inside looks.  **Defensive aggression is a real trade-off** Soft defence lets opponents shoot easier. Aggressive defence lowers opponent scoring in even matchups — typically by a few points per game — at the cost of more fouls, more opponent free throws, and more tiredness after the game.  **Sharper defence matchups** The primary defender on a shot is the player in the same court role as the shooter (point guard on point guard, and so on). Elite wing defence against their wing matters more than a team average used by v1.  **Height and build matter more** Rebound reach, rim contests, and paint finishing lean more on height and physique, not only the rebounding or defence rating on the card.
[2026-07-09 21:47] vachacz : ** Height, court role, and the position debate** I asked you whether we should punish playing out of position with a fixed matrix, or whether height and physique should do that job instead. Our answer in version 2 is height-first, not label-first.  Your card position (PG–C) is still the roster label you see everywhere. It does not slap a huge penalty on every skill when you line someone up elsewhere.  What does matter is where you put them on the court (the PG–C slot in your quarter lineup) and how tall they are compared to the matchup.  __Rebounds are the clearest example.__ Court slot on rebounds — where someone stands in your PG–C lineup changes how often they win the glass. A PG in the point-guard slot sits far from the rim and gets much less rebound reach than a center under the basket; wings and forwards sit in between. Even a high Rebounding rating rarely puts a PG on the same boards level as a big in the C circle. Reach also scales with height on top of slot. A short player in the center slot does not board like a tall true big — the gap is large, and slot and height stack.  Shooting and defence lean on height matchups and slot defence (your wing contests their wing). A tall forward in a big slot can work; a short guard in the center slot is a gimmick you should feel in the result.  We are not shipping a full cross-position skill penalty table in this release. If outsized lineups still feel wrong after friendlies, we will tune height and slot curves first.

[2026-09-10 22:19] vachacz : @everyone I would like to consult with you one possible change to the engine and tactics.  There were multiple requests of adding team tactics (often raised by <@1534801577951367179>).  I understand that ability of setting team tactics like zone defense or fast attack it very tempting but in the end they have to be modeled in the engine in a way that it's clear for the players and to the engine without overcomplicating and keeping the result visible in game stats. It's not that simple.  Alternative bit which can be way easier both for the engine and to grasp by the players are additional individual sliders. I see two candidates  **Defense area** possible to set on game tactics close to def focus on opponents players. It could shift defense between 2p and 3p. neutral slider is today's engine. rim defense is close to zone defense decreases opponents FG% for 2p but leaves 3p more open (e.g. +- 4-5%) and perimeter defense could work the other way around. Effect of Defense area could be multiplied by def focus.  another one I'm less sure about because offense has already 4 sliders is  **Driving frequency** allows player to take more unassisted shots after individual actions where passer quality plays no role. this idea is a bit fuzzy. it could involve more ball handling and athleticism both in offense and in defense    I suspect that with **Defense area** and potentially **Driving frequency** one could have very good control over player behaviour and team tactics would play lesser role in the game. Maybe we could entirely skip them.   Happy to hear your options. Especially faraone 😉

[2026-07-14 18:35] vachacz : @everyone creating this channel to discuss how we calibrate the academy. it got **+22 upvotes**. Below copy paste from the roadmap item  > Signing a prospect from a scout report halves your academy strength, and rebuilding from there back to 100% costs significant time and weekly investment — which makes signing feel like a heavy trade-off rather than a normal part of squad building, and can discourage players from using the academy pipeline at all. > Levers under consideration (not yet decided, may combine more than one): >  > - Increase scout report frequency from every 2 weeks to every 1 week — more chances to find a good prospect without touching the cost/strength economy at all. > - Make the academy cheaper overall, either by lowering the weekly investment cost needed to reach/hold a given strength level, or by increasing income elsewhere (e.g. ticket/gate revenue) so the existing cost feels lighter relative to the club's budget. > - Reduce the strength drop on signing (currently 50%) so a good pull doesn't set the academy back as far, allowing more frequent signings without as long a recovery. >  > Open question: these three levers interact — report frequency changes how often you're tempted to sign, cost changes how painful rebuilding is, and drop-% changes how far back a signing sets you. Tuning more than one at once risks overcorrecting (academy becomes a free lunch); worth deciding whether to ship one change and observe before stacking more.
[2026-07-14 18:36] vachacz : Second thing we will ship together which got **+14 upvotes **is rookie potential check  > When a scout report brings you three prospects, their skills show as a wide range (roughly 25 points wide) — enough to guess a build, but not enough to know if a junior is actually worth signing given how costly a signing is (halves your academy strength). Potential is fully hidden on top of that, so the decision to sign is largely a gamble. > Proposal: for a paid fee, send a prospect for additional medical testing before deciding whether to sign. This narrows their skill range from ~20 points down to ~10, and reveals a partial read on their potential — consistent with the transfer-market version of this feature (a range rather than an exact number, not a full reveal).

[2026-07-14 21:05] trainerrox : My two cents on the matter: I think everyone should have chances to pull a great rookie regardless of academy investments.   The game should be meant to be played by managers with different styles to improve chances of long-term popularity.   If the top rookies are locked behing heavy investments, they will end up only in the hands of managers committed to that play style, that will rarely sell them after such commitment, if ever. There would be no frequent chance to see bidwars for great talent.   Putting great rookies in the hands of managers "uninterested" to them, increases the chances to see them in the market, forces managers that chase them to compete with other with the same strategy in mind, you have to increase your balance via short/mid term market profit because at anytime a fierce bidwar could come up, that encourages game commitment and market interaction in a more compelling way than "I'll just max my academy and hope that my pulls are better than the others doing the same". On the other side, managers that don't care about rookie development would sure be happy with a huge amount of money coming from time to time off a lucky pull, allowing them to enjoy quick roster building through market spending, and it would make academy report day more interesting for everyone.   So I believe that hard capping rookie quality based on investment could lead to a more stale game, at the same time I think it's okay to guarantee higher odds to those willing to invest in it. I'm far from knowing what the correct numbers would be for a concrete implementation, but I think that the idea of random/uncapped rookie quality is worth exploring.

[2026-07-15 21:22] vachacz : After talking to my friend Claude we come to a conclusion that - either we make very small changes gradually (e.g. 1 week scout cadence + narrow down ranges for $$$ in the first step + maybe small economy adjustment) - or extend the system based on all feedbacks  I attach here a spec. I made a few iteration and I can imagine that this is an intersting option. Abstract below  - **Three-stage funnel **— Weekly scout report (3 candidates, fixed wide ranges) → youth squad (signed, not on senior roster) → first team (full reveal, matches). Max one signing per week; unpicked candidates are discarded with the next report. - **Reveal only after signing **— Report candidates show static ranges; potential stays hidden. In youth squad, ranges narrow via training + Analytics. Exact skills appear only on promotion. - **Three weekly spend channels (~200k total)** — Scouting shifts candidate quality; Analytics speeds range narrowing in youth; Coaching sets youth training speed (0.5×–1.5×). Each channel affects that week only — no accumulating academy level. - **Youth = training only** — No matches, no injuries, no senior roster slot. Faster development with Coaching; match experience waits until first team — the core keep-vs-promote trade-off.  Don't look at the numbers. They can be calibrated. Important is to discuss mechanics. Imho the idea is interesting because it does remove this accumulative effect which can generate lots of frustration. It also allows to pivot team strategy very quicly.

[2026-07-21 17:00] dcarra. : I think the current Academy system has an unintended side effect: it's dramatically reducing the number of young players available on the transfer market.  The main reason, in my opinion, is that the Academy's effectiveness drops by 50% after each pull. This creates a strong incentive to save every pull for the "perfect" prospect. After investing $2M or more into the Academy, most managers feel that using it on anything less than the best possible 16-year-old is a waste.  As a result, many managers delay promotions, and the only rookies that usually reach the market are the ones considered below average. This significantly reduces both the supply of young talent and the opportunities for trading and roster building.  If this is seen as a problem by others as well, here are a couple of possible directions:  1. Return to the old Charazay/MBT approach, where 16-year-olds were generated randomly and the Academy system is removed.  2. Replace the current percentage mechanic with a weekly operating cost. For example, managers could pay a weekly fee to choose the Academy's effectiveness level (e.g. $500k for 100%, $250k for 50%, etc.). This would make the decision about ongoing investment rather than encouraging everyone to hoard pulls for the perfect prospect.  These are only examples, and I'm sure better implementations could be found. My main concern is the current incentive structure: right now, it encourages managers to keep prospects in the Academy instead of promoting them, which ultimately leaves the transfer market with very few rookies available.

[2026-07-25 11:40] trainerrox : Hello everyone,  I tried to catch up with everything that has been written here over the past few days, and overall I really like the new academy implementations.  That said, I think these changes may increase the gap even further between newly generated rookies and some of the very strong players that were randomly assigned at the start of the game. To me, this feels like one of the biggest issues, and also one of the hardest to fix. Any change that lowers future player quality, even if it is a good change in isolation, can still create imbalance when compared to players already existing in the game world.  So I was wondering, <@1510400404708393120>, are you considering a game reset at some point? I saw you mentioned closing beta and moving to alpha around season 3, so I was curious whether that could potentially include a reset.  My humble opinion is that a reset would make sense if the goal is to properly stabilize the long-term balance of the game. In the meantime, I think it would be especially important to focus on the areas that are very hard to correct once the game has already progressed: player generation, academy balance, economy development, training scaling, and possibly other long-term systems.  On the other hand, aspects like the match engine, even if not perfect, feel easier to adjust later without permanently damaging the game world. But systems that affect player quality, money, and long-term progression need to be set up well from the start in order to keep the game enjoyable, varied, and engaging over time.  Thanks for reading, as always.

[2026-07-27 17:38] vachacz : @everyone let me share the concept for the next academy tuning I'm about to implement.  - so far I adjusted academy level progress curve (already live) - now it's time for tuning chances of getting certain potential  The concept is simple. Key characteristics and design ideas:  - chances for getting high potential grows with academy level - % distribution that nobody will pull <50% therefore P9/P10 start around 50% but are very unlikely - after reaching exact 100% you get a bonus of additional P8/P9/P10 chances (last line in the table) - to make it even more juicy I want to open add potential check to current academy feature Test. It will reveal ranges      - 1-3 --> low potential      - 4-7 --> decent potential       - 8-10 --> high potential (I considered putting 10 to separate category but It's not gonna happen) - there will be a rule that after reaching 99% next week there is guaranteed 100% because of flattening curve  Few principles behind this concept:  - waiting for 100% is expensive but there is an extra motivator of higher high pot chances - skill/pot reveal will make hard time for managers as you will have to decide whether to pull high potential junior at 80% or wait 3-4 more weeks  - as will have many high potential juniors most likely in the next calibration step I will calibrate junior starting skills  I'm convinced that this model will generate emotions while evaluating new scout reports and will prevent us from going 100% blindly ... despite the bonus which will make your decisions hard 🙂   Next post-implementation steps: - add some back-office metrics showing amount of pulled juniors, avg academy level, etc so that I can make adjustments based on data - calibrate starting skills of juniors and starting teams (quite likely lowering according to <@94888897875542016>'s suggestions)  - fine tune academy recovery time (with current curve I can do it fast)

And it's far from being a racist or something like that: in reality, most Afro-Ukrainians have names connected to their African heritage. [2026-08-18 09:53] vachacz : Let me explain that change a bit. Game has avatars divided into ethnic groups and then on country level there is a config defining proportion of ethnic groups in given country. By doing so we achieve the right mixture of avatars for given country. Example config for Poland and Brisil.      "BR": {       "name": "Brazil",       "region": "South America",       "weights": { "latino": 50, "black": 40, "caucasian_mediterranean": 8, "asian_north": 2 }     },     "PL": {       "name": "Poland",       "region": "Europe East",       "weights": { "caucasian_nordic": 93, "black": 5, "asian_north": 2 }     },  Those weights were generated by AI as I'm not a sociologist 😉 Surprisingly Ukraine had 10% black which was for sure too high and <@1519756993521389720> reported that. I know a lot of Ukrainians who moved to Poland and helps some of them settle down after the war started and I'm also confident that 10% was too high. There was no intention to discriminate anybody here, but I get the point and I understand importance of it. I'm sorry If anybody felt offended. My wording was really bad. I admit that.

[2026-09-15 18:49] carlomtlopes_69000 : 5.6. Fatigue Fatigue (0–100) is between games. It rises after each match and falls every night at midnight. It does not reset when a player sits — the bar tracks how worn down he is heading into the next fixture. At season rollover, every player’s fatigue bar resets to 0 (fresh for the new season).  After each match, fatigue gain for that player is:  minutes played × 0.19 × defense aggression multiplier × (1.5 − 0.008 × Stamina)  Each midnight, everyone recovers:  0.5 + 10% of current fatigue (same for every player — Stamina does not speed up recovery)  Friendlies: §1.2 (about 10% of league fatigue for the same minutes and aggression).  High weekly fatigue makes players less effective on field goals, free throws, rebounding, and passing — and it bites offence harder than defence (the green zone on the bar still means barely any effect). In-match injury risk also rises when someone keeps playing while tired (separate from the weekly bar — see §9.3). The §5.7 heavy-minutes rule is independent of the fatigue bar. How much the bar moves your skills in a fixture is §5.6.2.  5.6.1. Fatigue bar colours Zone    Fatigue    What it means 🟢 Green    0–20    Fresh enough — play him freely, minimal effect. 🟡 Yellow    20–40    Tiring — a noticeable dip; think about rotating. 🟠 Orange    40–60    Heavily fatigued — real penalty, rest him soon. 🔴 Red    60–100    Gassed — avoid playing if you can.
[2026-09-15 18:50] carlomtlopes_69000 : Portanto: 0.5 + 10% da tua fadiga atual de recuperação por noite

No máximo crescerá 20 cms:  Career height target — when a player joins the youth track (academy signing or your starting juniors), the game locks in a full-grown height somewhere inside that position's adult band. It is never below their height at that moment. It is also capped by how much they could still grow before turning 22: at most four centimetres per remaining youth season (rollovers while they are still 21 or younger). A 16-year-old has five such seasons ahead (ages 17–21 after joining), so current height plus 20 cm is the reach cap before the adult ceiling applies; a 17-year-old has four seasons (18–21), so plus 16 cm. You do not see the target number on a scout card or profile; you see it play out as they grow season by season.
